pages.title: Radar
pages.text: Because vanilla Minecraft ray tracing performs poorly—despite AeroIE's limited improvements—the Control Seat uses "causality" radar. Any existing subspace within detection range can be scanned.$(br2)The radar currently has a default range of 1024 blocks. Sable subspaces are less maneuverable than Valkyrien ships in unloaded chunks, so a more elaborate range model would offer little benefit.

Every detected subspace is marked on the HUD: red for hostile, green for friendly, and blue for unknown. See "Identification Friend or Foe" below.$(br2)If a hostile subspace is detected, the first one scanned becomes the locked target and receives an additional box marked "TGT."$(br2)Missiles and heavy turrets in automatic mode attack only the locked hostile target; ordinary turrets are not restricted this way. Press Comma to cycle between hostile targets.

pages.title: Identification Friend or Foe (IFF)
pages.text: The Control Seat identifies friend and foe from prefixes in each subspace's name—not its ID. Right-click the air with an IFF item to edit friendly and hostile name prefixes, then Shift-right-click the Control Seat to apply them. The HUD displays hostile subspaces in red, friendly subspaces in green, and unknown subspaces in blue. The name of the Control Seat's own subspace is automatically added as a friendly prefix.$(br2)Player-assembled subspaces have no name by default and are therefore marked as unnamed.
